channel.title: daryo
channel.description: Regional headlines in English, updated four times a day.

item.title: Uzbekistan is a driving force in the Organization of Turkic States, says Secretary General
item.description: Kubanychbek Omuraliev, Secretary General of the Organization of Turkic States, congratulated Uzbekistan on its 35th Independence Day. He highlighted Uzbekistan's significant contributions to the Turkic world's unity through initiatives in transport, trade, digital transformation, education, culture, and regional dialogue. Omuraliev noted Uzbekistan's reforms under President Shavkat Mirziyoyev have strengthened its international standing.

item.title: Kazakh President Tokayev congratulates Mirziyoyev on Uzbekistan's 35th Independence Day at SCO Summit
item.description: Kazakh President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev congratulated Uzbek President Shavkat Mirziyoyev and Kyrgyz President Sadyr Japarov on their countries' 35th independence anniversaries during the SCO summit in Kyrgyzstan. Tokayev thanked Kyrgyzstan for its hospitality and praised the SCO's growth into a major international organization over 25 years, emphasizing mutual trust and respect for sovereignty.

item.title: Uzbekistan President holds dialogue on improving business conditions
item.description: Uzbekistan's President Shavkat Mirziyoyev met with entrepreneurs in Khiva to discuss improving conditions for businesses. The focus shifted from supporting startups to fostering growth for existing enterprises, emphasizing access to finance, technology, markets, and a predictable regulatory environment. Business credit portfolios have nearly tripled.

item.title: Uzbekistan to revise social registry for targeted poverty reduction and expanded support
item.description: Uzbekistan will change its approach to identifying needy families and expand social support measures, President Shavkat Mirziyoyev announced. The national social protection agency will review the social registry system by year-end. The evaluation will shift to a multidimensional approach, considering chronic illnesses, disability, multiple children, and family members working abroad. Working mothers will receive benefits until their child turns one.

item.title: Four Uzbek citizens arrested in South Korea for allegedly financing Syrian terrorist group
item.description: Four Uzbek citizens have been arrested in South Korea on suspicion of financing terrorism. They are accused of providing financial support, including cryptocurrency and vehicles, to the "Katibah Tawhid wal Jihod" group operating in Syria. Investigations revealed one suspect purchased 11 used cars and two excavators for the group.

item.title: Uzbekistan to implement new poverty reduction and employment system
item.description: Uzbekistan will introduce a new system for poverty reduction and employment enhancement, announced President Shavkat Mirziyoyev. Regional and district poverty reduction headquarters will receive additional powers and resources totaling 3.2 trillion Uzbek soums. Local leaders will dedicate three days weekly to poverty and employment issues.

item.title: Uzbekistan to Implement New System for Poverty Reduction and Income Growth
item.description: Uzbekistan will introduce a completely new system to combat poverty and increase incomes, President Shavkat Mirziyoyev announced. Districts will receive 3.2 trillion soums, and local authorities will focus solely on poverty and employment issues three days a week. This approach was developed after analyzing poverty reduction strategies in Khorezm region.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan Faces Climate Crisis as Glaciers Melt, Causing Billions in Damage
item.description: Kyrgyzstan is confronting a climate crisis with rapidly melting glaciers, leading to significant damage. Temperatures are rising, glacier coverage has decreased by 16-17% since 2000, and glacial lake outburst floods pose increasing risks. The government is developing a National Adaptation Plan to manage climate risks.

item.title: Bobojon Ghafurov's book "Tajiks" published in German
item.description: To mark the 35th anniversary of Tajikistan's independence, Bobojon Ghafurov's seminal work "Tajiks" has been translated and published in German. The Ministry of Foreign Affairs reports this initiative aims to popularize the ancient culture of the Tajik people. International scholars praised the translation's timeliness and significance.

item.title: Uzbekistan Engages in High-Level Diplomatic Meetings with India, Azerbaijan, and Pakistan
item.description: Uzbekistan's foreign policy prioritizes trust and cooperation. Prime Minister Modi visited Uzbekistan for talks with President Mirziyoyev on August 29-30, focusing on trade, energy, and healthcare. Meetings also occurred between Azerbaijan and Armenia, and Uzbekistan and Pakistan, discussing economic and regional issues.

item.title: Tajikistan Promotes New Generals, Including Prison and Traffic Police Heads
item.description: Tajikistan has promoted several officials to new general ranks, including the heads of the prison system and the State Traffic Police Department. Some individuals have received their general's rank for the first time. The report indicates a reshuffling within high-ranking security and law enforcement positions.

item.title: Uzbekistan President tasks to lift 230,000 families out of poverty by end of 2026
item.description: President Shavkat Mirziyoyev has instructed to lift 230,000 families out of poverty by the end of 2026. Regional and district authorities must effectively organize their штаб operations. They are tasked with placing 350,000 people into permanent jobs and increasing the income of another million residents by December.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan allocates 20 million soms for flu vaccine in 2026
item.description: Kyrgyzstan has allocated 20 million soms for the purchase of flu vaccines for 2026, based on a request from the Department of Disease Prevention and State Sanitary and Epidemiological Surveillance. The funds will procure 63,733 doses, expected to arrive by October 1, 2026. Procurement plans for 2027 will be discussed in September.

item.title: Climate change may exacerbate poverty in Kyrgyzstan, disproportionately affecting vulnerable groups
item.description: Climate change in Kyrgyzstan is predicted to hit the most vulnerable hardest, including women, children, youth, the elderly, people with disabilities, and low-income families. Over 57% of the population relies on agriculture, making them susceptible to droughts, water scarcity, and land degradation, which can worsen social and economic inequality.

item.title: Bishkek and Osh Prepare for Climate Change Impacts by 2035
item.description: Bishkek and Osh are included in Kyrgyzstan's National Adaptation Plan through 2035 due to climate vulnerability. Measures address heat stress, overloaded utility systems, and infrastructure risks from heavy precipitation. Plans involve reviewing urban planning documents and implementing green infrastructure to mitigate climate impacts.

item.title: Uzbekistan to pay benefits until child turns one for working mothers, revises social registry
item.description: Uzbekistan will now pay benefits to working mothers until their child turns one year old. The system for including needy populations in a social registry is also being revised. Families in the registry will receive vouchers to cover kindergarten fees, training, transport, and dormitory costs.

item.title: Tajik President Awards State Honors to Security Personnel
item.description: On September 3, 2026, Tajikistan's President Emomali Rahmon presented state awards and special ranks to members of law enforcement, judicial, and military structures. The ceremony, held at the Palace of Nation, commemorated the 35th anniversary of Tajikistan's independence. Rahmon emphasized the role of armed forces and security bodies in safeguarding independence and national security.

item.title: Uzbekistan to Conduct Comprehensive Business Census from October 15 to November 30
item.description: Uzbekistan will conduct a large-scale business census from October 15 to November 30, 2026, to update information on active economic entities. The census aims to inventory businesses, determine their industry affiliation, and update statistical registers. This initiative addresses the significant issue of the unobserved economy, estimated at 23% of the country's GDP.

item.title: Uzbekistan Airways Flight Returns to Tashkent Due to Russian Airspace Restrictions
item.description: An Uzbekistan Airways flight bound for Russia was forced to return to Tashkent. This was due to temporary restrictions imposed by the Russian Federation on accepting aircraft at certain airports. Another flight from Termiz to Moscow was rerouted to St. Petersburg.

item.title: OPEC Fund to Lend Tajikistan $30 Million for Road Reconstruction in Gorno-Badakhshan
item.description: Tajikistan and the OPEC International Development Fund have signed a Strategic Partnership for 2026-2028. The first project involves reconstructing the Rushon-Vardzesh road in Gorno-Badakhshan Autonomous Province, funded by a $30 million loan from OPEC. This will upgrade 82.2 km of the Dushanbe-Kulma-China highway.

item.title: Uzbekistan to Replace Incompetent Mahalla Assistants with New Cadres
item.description: Uzbekistan plans to replace ineffective assistant mahalla (neighborhood) leaders with new, proactive individuals. Over 8,992 assistant positions will be filled. The most exemplary assistants will receive a special qualification level and up to a 50% bonus.

item.title: Uzbekistan Introduces New System: Governors to Focus on Poverty and Employment Three Days a Week
item.description: Uzbekistan is implementing a completely new system for addressing poverty. Governors will now dedicate three days per week to issues of poverty reduction and employment. This initiative aims to tackle poverty more effectively across the country.

item.title: Uzbek President Criticizes Ineffective Use of Poverty Reduction Funds
item.description: President Shavkat Mirziyoyev criticized the insufficient effectiveness of loan resources allocated for poverty reduction and increasing incomes. Despite 314 trillion soums allocated in three years, the impact on poverty reduction varies significantly across districts, with some districts showing much higher per-person spending than others.

item.title: Uzbek President Criticizes Regional Leaders for Lack of Business Acumen
item.description: President Shavkat Mirziyoyev criticized some regional leaders for lacking the knowledge or patience to create jobs. He noted that 62,000 people who received bank loans for businesses are struggling to repay them, highlighting the ineffectiveness of allocated credit resources across districts.

item.title: Number of Needy People in Uzbekistan Decreases to 1.5 Million
item.description: The number of needy people in Uzbekistan has decreased to 1.5 million. However, the president criticized district and mahalla officials for their hesitation and unwillingness to take responsibility for poverty and unemployment issues.

item.title: Uzbekistan's Central Bank to Strengthen Oversight of Bank Currency Risks and Asset Quality
item.description: Uzbekistan's Central Bank is tightening requirements for banks on reserves and currency risk management, while transitioning financial reporting to international standards. Central Bank Chairman Timur Ishmetov stated that the regulator is shifting focus from identifying future risks to enhancing the overall stability of the financial system.

item.title: SCO Countries to Conduct Joint Drills for Emergency Situations
item.description: Following a summit in Bishkek, Shanghai Cooperation Organisation (SCO) member states agreed to provide aid to countries affected by emergencies. Kyrgyzstan proposed a mechanism for this, while Russia suggested resource reserve funds. SCO nations will prioritize humanitarian assistance to members facing natural or man-made disasters.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan Begins Construction of Infectious Disease Research Center
item.description: Construction has commenced on a new scientific center for infectious disease research in Kyrgyzstan, according to the Ministry of Health. The facility aims to conduct laboratory research, scientific work, and train specialists to enhance the country's response to disease threats.

item.title: New judge appointed to Moskovsky District Court in Chui region
item.description: Artur Shadybekov has been appointed judge of the Moskovsky District Court of Chui region for a five-year term. He took the oath of office and officially assumed his duties following presidential decrees. Supreme Court Chairman Mederbek Satyev attended the ceremony.

item.title: Uzbekistan aims to attract more family tourists from India with new flights
item.description: Uzbekistan plans to increase tourist flow from India, focusing on family travel with children. Discussions are underway with Indian bloggers and influencers to promote Uzbekistan as a safe destination. New Hyderabad-Tashkent flights will launch on September 28, operating twice weekly.

item.title: Kyrgyz poet Akbar Ryskulov explains signing of 'letter of 75'
item.description: Kyrgyzstan's People's Poet and diplomat Akbar Ryskulov testified in court regarding the 'letter of 75'. He stated he signed the appeal for early presidential elections because he believed it aimed to develop the economy and ensure stability, seeing no ulterior motive.

item.title: Indian citizens can now enter Uzbekistan visa-free with valid visas from 8 countries
item.description: Starting September 1, 2026, Indian citizens with valid multiple-entry business or tourist visas from eight specific countries or Schengen states can enter Uzbekistan visa-free for up to 30 days. A return flight ticket is also required.

item.title: Tajikistan and South Korea's LS Corporation Discuss Energy Cooperation
item.description: Tajikistan's Minister of Energy and Water Resources met with representatives from South Korea's LS Corporation to discuss bilateral cooperation in the energy sector. The meeting focused on attracting investments and implementing joint projects, with Tajikistan presenting its energy sector investment opportunities.

item.title: Nearly 1 million hectares of unrecorded land clarified in Uzbekistan
item.description: As a result of the agricultural census, the boundaries and categories of 985,500 hectares of land, previously not reflected in records, have been clarified in Uzbekistan. Permanent statistical registers for agriculture will be formed.

item.title: Tajikistan and EU Discuss Industrial Cooperation, Focusing on Light Industry and Cotton Processing
item.description: Tajikistan's Minister of Industry met with the EU Ambassador to discuss industrial cooperation. Key areas included light industry development, textile production, and cotton processing. Both sides expressed readiness for continued dialogue and mutually beneficial collaboration.

item.title: Denmark Deploys Troops to Greenland Amidst Rising Tensions with US and Geopolitical Instability
item.description: Denmark has sent conscripted soldiers to Greenland for the first time in recent history, aiming to strengthen its Arctic position amid diplomatic friction with the US and regional geopolitical tensions.

item.title: Tashkent agency vows to prevent demolition of historic house on Bobur Street
item.description: Tashkent's Cultural Heritage Agency will prevent any illegal attempts to demolish or alter the historic house at 7 Bobur Street. The agency stated the building's status as a cultural heritage site will be maintained, and previous proposals to remove it from the national register were rejected.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan's AI-92 gasoline prices increased by nearly 1.5 percent in August
item.description: In August, AI-92 gasoline prices in Kyrgyzstan rose by 1.46 percent, reaching 89.11 soms per liter. AI-95 gasoline saw a 0.53 percent increase, costing 109.27 soms. Diesel fuel prices slightly decreased by 0.17 percent to 101.69 soms. Since the start of the year, gasoline prices have increased significantly.

item.title: Chingiz Kaziev appointed Deputy Chief of Staff of Kyrgyzstan's Parliament
item.description: Chingiz Kaziev has been appointed Deputy Chief of Staff of the Zhogorku Kenesh, Kyrgyzstan's parliament. Venera Kulataeva, the former Deputy Chief of Staff, is now the First Deputy Chief of Staff. These appointments were formalized by Marlen Mamataliev, the Speaker of the Zhogorku Kenesh.

item.title: Tajikistan and Iran discuss cooperation prospects for Sangtudinskaya HPP-2
item.description: On September 2, 2026, Dushanbe hosted a meeting between Tajikistan's Minister of Energy and Water Resources and the CEO of Iran's "Sangob" company. They discussed the current state and future prospects of cooperation in the energy sector, specifically regarding the Sangtudinskaya HPP-2.
